key_insight: A standardized time-lapse embryo imaging database plus a gradient boosting ensemble can improve blastocyst outcome prediction by combining zygote morphokinetics with conventional embryo assessment.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help IVF labs build more reproducible, data-driven embryo selection tools that capture information missed by morphology alone.
method: Built a database of 631 2PN zygotes from 218 IVF cycles with standardized time-lapse imaging and annotations.
Extracted 84 zygote-stage morphokinetic features and 8 conventional embryo assessment features.
Trained a LightGBM-based fusion model with recursive feature elimination and nested five-fold cross-validation.
evidence_signal: In ablation testing, the full fusion model achieved AUC 0.78, outperforming morphokinetics-only (0.71) and conventional-only (0.65) models.
watch_item: The model is based on a single-center retrospective dataset, so broader validation is needed before routine clinical implementation.
paper_title: Construction of a Standardized Time-Lapse Imaging Database and a Gradient Boosting Ensemble Framework for Integrating Zygote Morphokinetic Parameters with Conventional Embryo Assessment
